passages.title: Succession of Leadership.
passages.text: In these final chapters, leadership passes from Moses to Joshua and the covenant is written down.

notes.text: On God as the Rock, see vv. 15, 18, 30–31; also Ps. 18:2.
no longer his children. See note on 14:1–2. Compare Hos. 1:9. crooked and twisted generation. See Phil. 2:15.
your father. See v. 5. The notion of God as father of his people is rare in the OT. Compare note on 14:1–2.
gave to the nations their inheritance. For example, Edom, Moab, and Ammon in 2:1–23, as well as Israel throughout the book. the Lord’s portion. A term of special affection. See note on 4:20.
Bashan was a particularly fertile area, where Og had been king (3:1–11).

Jeshurun means “the upright one.” It was a poetic name for Israel (see Isa. 44:2) but is used sarcastically here. jealousy with strange gods. See Deut. 4:24 and note on 4:23–24. Throughout Deuteronomy, idolatry is seen as the most serious sin and the greatest threat to the nation (see also 32:21). God, the Rock, has redeemed Israel; idols or false gods have no real existence (v. 17).
hide my face. Often, God’s punishment of sin is his withdrawal from the sinner (v. 18).
depths of Sheol. The place of the dead.
God will not punish his people forever, lest their adversaries should misunderstand, and think that he is unable to save his people. Compare 9:28.
If they were wise, they would understand. Israel would fall far short of the ideal of demonstrating a godly wisdom that is admired by other nations (as described in 4:6–8).
Israel’s Rock is God. The rock of the enemies refers to the so-called gods of other nations, who are nothing. Hence the enemies are by themselves.
Vengeance is mine, and recompense. God will judge the wicked. For the Lord will vindicate his people. Beyond defeat and exile, God will restore his people (30:1–3).
I, even I, am he. The repetition of “I” emphasizes God’s sovereignty (compare Ex. 3:14). no god beside me. See Deut. 4:35; 5:7; and note on 4:35–36.
The song ends in triumph. In spite of Israel’s sin and exile, God will ultimately restore them.
it is . . . your very life. Compare “he is your life”; 30:19–20.
Like a patriarch, Moses blesses Israel before his death.
Abarim, Mount Nebo. See 34:1. Aaron your brother died in Mount Hor. See 10:6 and Num. 20:24–28. you broke faith with me. See Num. 20:11–13.
